landability_note: Backend-only Rust edit confined to a single reality-server route file (routes/imports.rs) plus an optional shared const; no migration and no client/openapi regen (the ImportJobsQuery wire shape is unchanged - only the server-side clamping of an already-optional limit param). Remedy: replace `query.limit.unwrap_or(20)` at routes/imports.rs:124 with `query.limit.unwrap_or(20).clamp(1, MAX_IMPORT_JOBS_LIMIT)` (mirroring the sibling list handlers, e.g. agencies.rs:127 `query.limit.unwrap_or(50).clamp(1, 200)`), reusing the same max the other reality-server list routes use. Verifiable via `cargo build -p reality-server` plus a focused unit/integration test asserting (i) `?limit=-1` no longer reaches SQL / no longer 500s, and (ii) `?limit=100000` is capped to the max page size.

evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/imports.rs:115-134 - list_import_jobs (GET /api/v1/imports/jobs, authenticated PortalPrincipal) passes the user-supplied page size straight through as `query.limit.unwrap_or(20)` with NO `.clamp(...)`. The adjacent OFFSET on the very same call IS clamped (`crate::util::clamp_offset_i32(query.offset)` at :125), so the limit is the only unbounded pagination input on this endpoint.

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal/imports.rs:36-69 - the repo binds that i32 limit directly into `... ORDER BY j.created_at DESC LIMIT $3 OFFSET $4` via `.bind(limit)` and `fetch_all`. Two concrete failure modes: (1) a NEGATIVE limit (e.g. `?limit=-1`) reaches Postgres, which raises `ERROR: LIMIT must not be negative`, surfaced only as a generic 500 via `crate::util::errors::db_error("list import jobs", e)` - an unhandled-error-on-user-input path; (2) an OVERSIZED limit (e.g. `?limit=2000000000`) removes the page bound entirely, so the whole result set for that user is materialized into a Vec by fetch_all.

Asymmetry confirming this is an accidental omission, not intent: EVERY other paginated reality-server list route clamps the user limit - agencies.rs:127 `.unwrap_or(50).clamp(1,200)`, agent_reviews.rs:113 `.unwrap_or(20).clamp(1,100)`, realtors.rs:204 `.unwrap_or(20).clamp(1,100)`, portal_listings.rs:431 `.unwrap_or(20).clamp(1,100)`, articles.rs:155 `.unwrap_or(20).clamp(1,100)`, saved_searches.rs:324-327 `.clamp(1, ALERTS_MAX_LIMIT=200)`, listings.rs clamp_pagination `.clamp(1, MAX_LISTINGS_LIMIT=100)` - and the sibling endpoint in the SAME module, agency_imports.rs:175 list_import_history, uses a hardcoded `LIMIT 100`. list_import_jobs is the lone outlier.

Dedup/tracking status: NOT a duplicate of the done backlog row code-review-reality-server-pagination-offset-overflow (resolved by PR #2921, 2026-09-01). That sweep added MAX_LIST_OFFSET + clamp_offset/clamp_offset_i32 and applied them to all 9 OFFSET params - which is exactly why list_import_jobs:125 clamps its offset today while leaving the adjacent limit unbounded. The LIMIT clamp was missed by that offset-only sweep and is tracked by no existing backlog item (the only reality-server code-review rows are inquiry-detail-empty-messages and saved-search-watermark-discard, both unrelated). Fresh, still-live on 2026-10-21.

Severity MEDIUM (+2): authenticated and self-scoped (`WHERE j.user_id = $1`), so no cross-tenant leak and the oversized-limit result set is bounded by the caller's own import-job count - DoS amplification is limited. But the negative-limit -> 500 is a concrete, deterministic bug on a user-facing endpoint, and the missing bound is a clear regression gap from the PR #2911/#2921 clamp sweep. Confidence medium: the full route->repo->SQL bind path is confirmed by static read; the negative-limit 500 is deterministic from Postgres LIMIT semantics but not runtime-confirmed in this pass (no execution per static-only rule).
